Using the visual schematic above for the Cartesian product ${A}^{2}$ for $A={p,q,r},$ determine which of the following statements are true.

- $(q,q)\in {A}^{2}$
- $(p,r)\in {A}^{2}$
- ${q}^{2}\in {A}^{2}$
worked_solution:
The set ${A}^{2}$ is equivalent to the Cartesian product $A\times A.$

The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

To complete our schematic of $A\times A,$ we write an ordered pair whose first coordinate is the corresponding element of the first set $(A)$ and the second coordinate is the corresponding element of the second set $(A)$ at each intersection.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/919ad6e16dcd1d8f02e8c15c7bd1dfa15f67232c99706dfbc1239e1f9a0f99e5.png)

According to our diagram:

- $(q,q)\in {A}^{2}\,✓$

- $(p,r)\in {A}^{2}\,✓$

- ${q}^{2}\in {A}^{2}\,\times $

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
